paragraphs: On Thursday after school, Tom and Ben stood on the football field with Coach Matt. The sky was blue, and the field was warm and dry. The sun was low, and the boys had their football shoes on. Coach Matt held his silver whistle in one hand and a list in the other. The team was ready, but one boy was not there. "Where is Hugo?" asked Coach Matt. "He is always the first guy on the field." "Is anybody able to call him?"

"He sent a message to my mom's phone," said Ben. He took out the phone and read it. Ben read the message slowly, and a smile came to his face. "Hi, Ben. I am not able to come to practice today." "I am at the hospital with my dad." "Please tell Coach. Do not worry, I am fine." "I am so glad, and I cannot stop smiling."

Tom looked at Ben, because Hugo never missed a practice. "Is he sick?" he asked. "No," said Ben. "He sent a photo too." "Look at this." The photo showed a white door and a blue sign with the words "Birth Center." Under the sign, a very small hand held Hugo's finger. Tom and Coach Matt looked at the screen, and nobody spoke for a moment.

"Is that a real hand?" asked Tom. "Of course," said Ben. "It is very small, but it is strong." "Hugo is a funny guy, but this is not a game." Coach Matt looked at the photo for a long time. Then he smiled and gave the phone back. "Good," he said. "That is the best reason to miss practice."

"Coach, do you know what it is?" asked Tom. "I think so," said Coach Matt. "Anyway, let us not say it before Hugo does." "We will wait for his news." Ben put the phone in his bag. Tom looked at the empty place on the field where Hugo usually stood. "What do we do today?" he asked.

"Today we will have a short and relaxing practice," said Coach Matt. "We will play a game with no running." "After that, each of you will write a card for Hugo's family." "What do we write?" asked Tom. "Something kind," said Coach Matt, "and something short." He used his whistle once, and the game began.

sentences.text: On Thursday after school, Tom and Ben stood on the football field with Coach Matt.
The sky was blue, and the field was warm and dry.
The sun was low, and the boys had their football shoes on.
Coach Matt held his silver whistle in one hand and a list in the other.
The team was ready, but one boy was not there.
"Where is Hugo?" asked Coach Matt.
"He is always the first guy on the field."
"Is anybody able to call him?"
"He sent a message to my mom's phone," said Ben.
He took out the phone and read it.
Ben read the message slowly, and a smile came to his face.
"Hi, Ben. I am not able to come to practice today."
"I am at the hospital with my dad."
"Please tell Coach. Do not worry, I am fine."
"I am so glad, and I cannot stop smiling."
Tom looked at Ben, because Hugo never missed a practice.
"Is he sick?" he asked.
"No," said Ben.
"He sent a photo too."
"Look at this."
The photo showed a white door and a blue sign with the words "Birth Center."
Under the sign, a very small hand held Hugo's finger.
Tom and Coach Matt looked at the screen, and nobody spoke for a moment.
"Is that a real hand?" asked Tom.
"Of course," said Ben.
"It is very small, but it is strong."
"Hugo is a funny guy, but this is not a game."
Coach Matt looked at the photo for a long time.
Then he smiled and gave the phone back.
"Good," he said.
"That is the best reason to miss practice."
"Coach, do you know what it is?" asked Tom.
"I think so," said Coach Matt.
"Anyway, let us not say it before Hugo does."
"We will wait for his news."
Ben put the phone in his bag.
Tom looked at the empty place on the field where Hugo usually stood.
"What do we do today?" he asked.
"Today we will have a short and relaxing practice," said Coach Matt.
"We will play a game with no running."
"After that, each of you will write a card for Hugo's family."
"What do we write?" asked Tom.
"Something kind," said Coach Matt, "and something short."
He used his whistle once, and the game began.
